summary:
HUMANS IN SPACE is an interactive educational game that introduces players to the challenges of designing and managing space missions, combining science, technology, engineering, and strategic decision-making through realistic space exploration scenarios. Players take on the role of mission designers—tailoring missions to their own interests—and make decisions based on scientific objectives and limited resources, such as mass, energy, budget, data, communications, and time. Through scenarios like rescuing a satellite, traveling to Mars, or building a lunar base, participants experiment, solve problems, and learn from the consequences of their own decisions.

The game integrates real-time NASA data via an API, displaying six space weather indicators: solar flares (FLR), coronal mass ejections (CME), geomagnetic storms (GST), solar energetic particles (SEP), and interplanetary shocks (IPS), among others.

Developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Supabase, and PostgreSQL, the project utilizes AI-assisted development tools.

Led by 11-year-old Betito Bascuñan, the project draws on his experience participating in hackathons, the Argentine Aerospace Club, and The Mars Society Argentina, as well as his role in founding ACEMA Cuyo—a regional branch of the Association for Experimental Rocketry and Space Modeling.

Created by children for children, and guided by experienced specialists, the goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers, scientists, engineers, and creators.
details:
HUMANS IN SPACE is an interactive educational game that introduces players to the challenges involved in designing and managing space missions.

Players take on the role of mission designers, exploring how scientific objectives influence engineering decisions. The project focuses on scenarios such as rescuing a lost satellite, launching a mission to Mars, or establishing a base on the Moon. Players must account for mission requirements and various resources, including mass, energy, budget, data, communications, and time.

The goal of the game is to make complex space-related concepts understandable through experimentation, decision-making, and problem-solving. Its educational approach encourages players to test different alternatives, understand the consequences, and learn from the outcomes of each mission.

HUMANS IN SPACE is designed to connect diverse interests with space exploration, demonstrating that science and technology require creativity, teamwork, and a varied skill set.

It also incorporates real-world data from NASA—accessed via API—such as space weather, providing real-time information on six variables: solar flares (FLR), coronal mass ejections (CME), geomagnetic storms (GST), solar energetic particles (SEP), and interplanetary shocks (IPS).

The project was developed using Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript 5.7, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Supabase, PostgreSQL, Vercel, GitHub, SWR, and Lucide React. AI-assisted tools were used during development, with their contributions noted throughout the project where applicable.

The project is led by 11-year-old Betito Bascuñan, who is establishing the Cuyo region branch of the Experimental Rocketry Association (ACEMA). He is a member of the Argentine Aerospace Club, has been involved with The Mars Society Argentina, has won several local hackathons, and has been engaged in space-related activities since the age of six.

Created by children for children—with guidance from experienced specialists—HUMANS IN SPACE seeks to inspire the next generation of space explorers, scientists, engineers, and creators.
